name: 🔐 Authentication

request.description:
Exchanges a one-time **grant token** (authorization code) for an `access_token` and a
long-lived `refresh_token`.

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Endpoint** | `POST https://{{accounts-domain}}/oauth/v2/token` |
| **Grant type** | `authorization_code` |
| **Returns** | `access_token`, `refresh_token`, `expires_in`, `api_domain` |

Paste your grant token into the **code** field. `redirect_uri` is disabled by default — enable
it for a Server-based Application, leave it off for a Self Client.

> The test script stores `access-token`, `refresh-token` and `expiry-time` in the active
> environment, so no manual copying is needed.

📘 [Generating tokens ↗](https://www.zoho.com/analytics/api/v2/authentication/generating-token.html)

Mints a fresh `access_token` from the stored refresh token. Access tokens expire after
**one hour** (`expires_in: 3600`); the refresh token itself does not change.

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Endpoint** | `POST https://{{accounts-domain}}/oauth/v2/token` |
| **Grant type** | `refresh_token` |
| **Returns** | `access_token`, `expires_in` |

> A user may hold at most **20 refresh tokens** per client — creating a 21st silently deletes
> the oldest.

📘 [Refreshing the access token ↗](https://www.zoho.com/analytics/api/v2/authentication/refresh-token.html)

Permanently invalidates a refresh token. Any access token already issued from it stops
working once it expires.

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Endpoint** | `POST https://{{accounts-domain}}/oauth/v2/token/revoke` |
| **Body** | `token=<refresh_token>` |

> Use this when a user disconnects your integration, or when a token may have leaked.

📘 [Revoking a refresh token ↗](https://www.zoho.com/analytics/api/v2/authentication/revoke-token.html)

description:
# 🔐 Authentication

Every Zoho Analytics REST API v2 call is authenticated with an **OAuth 2.0 access token**.
Run the three requests in this folder once, and the rest of the collection works — the test
scripts write `access-token`, `refresh-token` and `expiry-time` into your active environment
automatically.

> The collection sends `Authorization: Bearer {{access-token}}` at collection level.
> Zoho also documents the equivalent `Authorization: Zoho-oauthtoken <token>` scheme; either
> is accepted.

### Setup, once

| Step | What to do |
| ---: | :--- |
| 1 | Register a client in the [Zoho API Console](https://api-console.zoho.com) — *Server-based Application* for web apps, *Self Client* for server-to-server. |
| 2 | Put `client-id`, `client-secret` and `redirect-uri` into your Postman environment. |
| 3 | Set `accounts-domain` and `analytics-domain` to **your data centre** (see the collection overview). |
| 4 | Generate a grant token (authorization code) and paste it into **Generate Tokens › code**. |

### Requests in this section

| # | Request | Purpose |
| ---: | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | **Generate Tokens** | Exchanges a grant token for an access token + refresh token. |
| 2 | **Refresh Access Token** | Mints a new access token from the refresh token. Access tokens live **1 hour**. |
| 3 | **Revoke Refresh Token** | Invalidates the refresh token and ends the session. |

### Scopes

Request the union of the scopes used by the endpoints you call — each request in this
collection lists its scope. `ZohoAnalytics.<family>.all` covers read/create/update/delete for
one family; `ZohoAnalytics.fullaccess.all` covers everything. Prefer the narrowest set.

> ⚠️ **Tokens are region bound.** A token issued by `accounts.zoho.eu` is rejected by
> `analyticsapi.zoho.com` with error `8535`.

📘 [Authentication guide ↗](https://www.zoho.com/analytics/api/v2/authentication.html)
